claims.text: An initially single-phase high-entropy alloy can undergo grain-boundary decohesion under high-strain-rate loading.
High-strain-rate loading can dynamically amorphize an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy.
High-strain-rate loading produces extreme grain refinement in the target alloy.
Extreme grain refinement causes grain-boundary decohesion and dynamic amorphization.
Ultra-nanocrystalline high-entropy alloys can exhibit inverse Hall–Petch softening.
Grain-boundary decohesion can occur in a solid-solution high-entropy alloy without significant grain-boundary segregation or phase separation.
Grain-boundary decohesion leads to toughness degradation and brittle behavior.
Dynamic amorphization leads to toughness degradation and brittle behavior.
Inverse Hall–Petch behavior causes toughness degradation and brittle behavior.
The proposed brittle behavior is relevant under both high- and low-temperature conditions and various loading conditions.
Conventional-alloy toughness loss is associated with grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation.
The proposed test compares high-entropy-alloy specimens with and without grain-boundary decohesion and dynamic amorphization under high-strain-rate loading.
Toughness, ductility, grain-boundary decohesion, and dynamic amorphization are to be measured.
The hypothesis is declared falsified if an alloy without decohesion and amorphization has toughness and ductility similar to a conventional alloy.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis states that extreme grain refinement causes decohesion and amorphization, but the structured fields place decohesion and amorphization as the mediator and grain refinement/inverse Hall–Petch behavior as the downstream mechanism, reversing the stated causal order.

The design proposes a direct comparison between high-entropy alloys with and without the proposed mediator, whereas the falsification rule instead compares the mediator-free high-entropy alloy with a conventional alloy. That outcome does not directly test the designed with-versus-without contrast.
